title: Juniper and the Witness
premise: Theo Zhou has spent two decades as the concierge of the Meridian Hotel in the coastal town of Juniper Hollow, cataloguing its secrets with the precision of a librarian. When a nervous stranger named Ada Voss pays a month in advance and begs Theo to prevent a murder she insists is scheduled for the solstice, Theo dismisses it as fantasy—until Ada vanishes and a body surfaces that matches her warning almost exactly. Digging into the town's oldest files, Theo discovers the murder is a reenactment of an unsolved death from thirty years ago, one her own late mentor may have helped cover up. To stop the second killing, Theo must expose the first, forcing the town's founding families to choose between their inherited silence and her inherited duty to the truth.
about_author: Lior Marchetti is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent a decade collecting the strange confessions guests make at 3 a.m. They write mysteries from a rented room above a defunct seaside hotel, where they still alphabetize the mail of strangers who never return.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Things
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo introduces the Meridian Hotel and her private ledger of guests' habits, debts, and lies—a system inherited from her mentor, Ruth. The emotional beat is quiet pride in being the town's invisible memory, shadowed by the anniversary of Ruth's death.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A rain-soaked stranger, Ada Voss, checks in, pays a month upfront in cash, and asks Theo to help her stop a murder that 'hasn't happened yet.' Theo refuses, but logs the request. The beat is unease—the first crack in Theo's orderly world.

chapters.title: The Solstice Warning
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Ada leaves a note naming the victim: Councilman Elias Brandt, dead on the solstice, 'as before.' Theo checks the town archives and finds a matching unsolved drowning from thirty years prior. The beat shifts from skepticism to dread.

chapters.title: Room 214, Vacant
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Ada misses checkout. Her room is scrubbed clean, paid through the month, and the front desk camera conveniently failed. Theo realizes someone at the hotel erased Ada. The beat is betrayal—the hotel itself is compromised.

chapters.title: The Brandt File
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo pulls Ruth's oldest files and finds pages razored out of the 1994 drowning case. Ruth knew the victim, Lena Marsh, personally. The beat is a shaken sense of inheritance: her mentor was part of the silence.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Theo. At the founders' annual dinner, Theo observes the old families—Brandt, Okafor, and the late Marshes—performing thirty years of cordiality. Elias Brandt is charming and terrified. The beat is theatrical tension beneath polished surfaces.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A body matching Ada's warning washes up—but it's not Elias. It's a drifter wearing Elias's missing watch. The murder has begun, but the script is already wrong. The beat is horror and confusion.

chapters.title: Alibis, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo cross-references every founder's alibi for both the old drowning and last night. Each alibi is airtight and each corroborates another's—too perfectly. The beat is the thrill of the hunt meeting the smell of conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Deputy Marisol Quintero, the one honest officer, warns Theo off the case—then quietly shares that the 1994 investigation was closed from above. The beat is cautious alliance between two women who keep records.

chapters.title: Ada's Voice Mail
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A delayed voice mail from Ada surfaces: she is Ruth's estranged daughter and came to finish her mother's confession. The razored pages were Ruth's. The beat is grief reframed—Ada is family by paper if not by blood.

chapters.title: The Okafor Cellar
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Following a ledger clue, Theo searches the Okafor wine cellar and finds Lena Marsh's missing diary, kept by Amara Okafor out of guilt. It names a fourth person present the night Lena died. The beat is revelation with a cost—Amara knows Theo was there.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Thursdays
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The diary reveals Lena was being blackmailed over an inheritance scheme that built half the town's fortunes. The fourth name is smudged, but the handwriting is Ruth's. The beat is the collapse of Theo's idolization of her mentor.

chapters.title: A Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Elias Brandt offers Theo a lifetime position and Ruth's sealed letters if she hands over the diary. He admits he was there in 1994 but claims he only watched. The beat is temptation and the taste of complicity.

chapters.title: The Watchmaker's Apprentice
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo traces the drifter's watch to a repair shop and learns someone commissioned a replica weeks ago—someone planning the reenactment down to the props. The killer is staging, not improvising. The beat is the killer becoming a presence, not a theory.

chapters.title: Missing Pages, Missing Girl
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Amara Okafor is found unconscious; the diary is gone. Ada is spotted alive at the ferry terminal and vanishes again. The killer is tying off loose ends exactly as the solstice approaches. The beat is escalating panic.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo deciphers Ruth's coded ledger margins: Ruth helped hide the body to protect her lover, the fourth founder, and has been paying blackmail ever since. The 'murder to come' is the final payment. The beat is devastating inheritance—Theo is living inside her mentor's debt.

chapters.title: The Fourth Founder
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The fourth name belongs to hotel owner Vivienne Cross, Theo's current employer and Ruth's lover. Vivienne admits everything calmly—she has been staging the reenactment to finally destroy the blackmailers, Ada included. The beat is the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo and Marisol lay a trap at the boathouse where Lena died, feeding Vivienne false word that Ada will be there. Elias, spooked, decides to confess publicly at midnight. The beat is coiled, breath-held preparation.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The trap springs wrong: Vivienne anticipated it, and Theo ends up alone with her among the tide-slick pilings as the water rises. Vivienne offers Theo Ruth's place in the town's protected silence. The beat is the climax's moral crucible.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo refuses—and reveals she has spent the night broadcasting Vivienne's confession on the hotel's ancient PA system to the gathered solstice crowd. Marisol makes the arrest as the town listens. Ada appears, alive, having fed Theo the final clue. The beat is cathartic exposure.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: POV Theo. In the aftermath, the town convulses: resignations, a reopened 1994 case, Lena Marsh's name on the memorial wall. Theo testifies to Ruth's role, grieving the mentor she can no longer unsee. The beat is the painful price of truth.

chapters.title: Concierge, Still
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Months later, Theo keeps the desk under new, honest management, and Ada takes a long-term room. Theo starts a fresh ledger with a first entry that is simply the truth. The beat is belonging earned—not inherited, but chosen.
